why: the B1 matrix registers the raw sha256 of its own source files as evidence, so 'blob == worktree bytes' must survive a fresh checkout; with core.autocrlf=true and no eol attribute a checkout injects CRLF and the registered hashes become unreproducible

measured_evidence.method: git archive --format=tar HEAD <path>, extract, compare byte length and sha256 against the worktree file

C-VRP_Cold-chainVehicleRoutingProblem/sc.note: pinned by the Green Phase .gitattributes; proves the pin mechanism works

pin_set.scoping_note: only the registered byte containers are pinned; a blanket '* -text' was rejected because 34 CRLF *.sh files under scripts/ would have their blobs rewritten

superseded_record_not_rewritten.action: the Green Phase identity file is NOT rewritten (it stays byte-intact as the record of that commit); this file carries the current pin-set hash forward as a new version
superseded_record_not_rewritten.reason: the pin set grew from 6 to 8 files, which necessarily changes the .gitattributes content

verification_required_after_commit: git archive HEAD <each pinned path> must reproduce the registered sha256 exactly; run after the commit that adds these pins, because git archive reads attributes from the committed tree
